entry.name: xnano
entry.description: A declarative terminal framework for Python built on ratatui & ratzilla.
entry.line: - [xnano](https://github.com/hsaeed3/xnano) - A declarative terminal framework for Python built on ratatui & ratzilla.

evidence.observation: 'An extremely nano terminal experience for Python, built on ratatui.' Layout and drawing run in Rust on ratatui. All of ratatui's widgets are in xnano.widgets. WebAssembly is supported via Pyodide. No mention of ratzilla.
Workspace members are xnano-terminal-cells/state/runtime/core/audio/image. Workspace dependencies include ratatui 0.30 and ratatui-core 0.1. No ratzilla.
The xnano terminal runtime depends on ratatui, ratatui-core and termprofile[ratatui]. No ratzilla, and none in the other member manifests checked.
Says v1 is no longer part of the current library and main is completely v2. v1 source lives on the v1 branch; last v1 release is 1.2.3.
v1: 'A simple python tui framework built on top of ratatui and tachyonfx'; 'incredibly declarative TUI framework'. No ratzilla.
The v1 core depends on ratatui 0.30, ratatui-core 0.1 and tachyonfx 0.25. No ratzilla.
The v1 Web host runs an offscreen runtime and streams cell frames to the browser. It says there is no separate HTML paint backend and does not mention ratzilla.

limitations: Git history was not searched exhaustively. A GitHub commit search for 'ratzilla' returned 0 results, but an earlier revision may have used Ratzilla.
Did not run the software.
Did not assess the legacy v1 branch's maintenance status. It exists, and the docs point users to release 1.2.3.
assessment.newDescription: A terminal framework for Python built on Ratatui.
assessment.reason: xnano is still a Python terminal framework built on Ratatui. The README says 'built on ratatui', shows the Built With Ratatui badge, and exposes all of ratatui's widgets in xnano.widgets. The workspace crates depend on ratatui 0.30, ratatui-core and PyO3 bindings. However, the claim 'built on … ratzilla' is unsupported: no mention of ratzilla appears in the root Cargo.toml, any of the 6 workspace member manifests, the pyproject files, the README, the docs index, or the v1 web docs. The legacy v1 branch's xnano-core/Cargo.toml uses ratatui and tachyonfx, not ratzilla. Browser support is now through Pyodide/WebAssembly with an in-memory canvas. The word 'declarative' described the legacy v1 ('incredibly declarative TUI framework'). The current main-branch v2 is described as 'a terminal you put things on', with imperative-style writes that stay live. The suggested wording drops the unsupported claims.

source.description: an extremely nano python terminal experience; built on ratatui.

entry.name: binsider

entry.name: termscp
entry.description: A feature rich terminal UI file transfer and explorer with support for SCP/SFTP/FTP/S3/SMB.
entry.section: Remote Access, APIs, and File Transfer
entry.line: - [termscp](https://github.com/veeso/termscp) - A feature rich terminal UI file transfer and explorer with support for SCP/SFTP/FTP/S3/SMB.

evidence.observation: description = "termscp is a feature rich terminal file transfer and explorer with support for SCP/SFTP/FTP/Kube/S3/GCS/SMB/WebDAV"; depends on tuirealm = "4" and remotefs-gcs/remotefs-smb.
Features list: SFTP, SCP, FTP and FTPS, Kube, S3, Google Cloud Storage (GCS), SMB, WebDAV.
tuirealm 4.1.0 depends on ratatui = { version = "0.30" }.

limitations: A shorter wording that names fewer protocols and ends with "and more" would date more slowly; the maintainer may prefer that.
